title: Unique normalized lax structure on the actual pro-etale section direct image
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $X,Y$ be schemes in universe $u$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be any scheme morphism. Use the fixed small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with objects and module sections in universe $u+1$ and morphisms in universe $u$. Write $R_T$ for the section-ring sheaf of the pulled-back coefficients on $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use exactly the coefficient map $c:R_Y\to f_*R_X$, section-module functors $L=f^*_{\rm sec}$ and $P=f_{*,\rm sec}$ and specified adjunction $L\dashv P$ of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Module tensors are the sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and their units are the regular modules $R_T$. A lax monoidal structure on $P$ consists of natural maps $\mu_{H,K}:PH\otimes_{R_Y}PK\to P(H\otimes_{R_X}K)$ and $e:R_Y\to PR_X$ satisfying associativity and the two unit identities. Call it normalized when for every $R_X$-module sheaves $H,K$, object $V$ of the small site of $Y$, and $x\in H(V\times_YX)$, $y\in K(V\times_YX)$, $\mu_{H,K}$ sends the local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ over $V$ to the local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ over $V\times_YX$, using the pure-tensor sections of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. There exists exactly one normalized lax monoidal structure on $P$. Its unit satisfies $e_V(r)=c_V(r)$ for every $V$ and $r\in R_Y(V)$; this unit formula is a conclusion, not an assumption on competing normalized structures.

proof.text: Set $C=Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $D=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $v(V)=V\times_YX$, $R=R_Y$ and $S=R_X$. By [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], precomposition along $v$ is the actual sheaf direct image. Both sites are small in the common module-section universe $u+1$, as stipulated in the statement. By [def-pd-section-module-operations-data], the specified functor $P$ is precisely this precomposition followed by scalar restriction along the fixed ring-sheaf map $c$: $(PH)(V)=H(vV)$, $r\cdot x=c_V(r)x$, and $P$ acts on maps by their components at $vV$. Thus the data satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-pd-ringed-direct-image-pairing-lax], with exactly the given coefficient map; no change of adjunction or coefficient category is involved.

source.place: Tags 03D6, definition-pushforward, and 03EK, section-tensor-product (Hom/Bilin display); specialization to the fixed pro-etale section operations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pd-ringed-direct-image-pairing-lax] to these data. Its tensors are the sheafified balanced tensors of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and its units are $R_Y,R_X$. Its unique lax structure supplies natural tensor maps and all three coherence identities. By [def-pd-section-module-operations-data], the pure tensor used here is the balanced section tensor followed by module sheafification and its canonical tensor identification. Consequently the normalization in the cited theorem is exactly the normalization in this item on every $V,x,y$. Every competing normalized lax structure therefore satisfies that theorem's uniqueness predicate, so equals the structure obtained above. The same theorem concludes $e_V(r)=c_V(r)$ for every $V,r$ without assuming a unit formula for competing structures, giving the final clause.
